changelog:
# JediCoop patch notes

## 0.30.5

**Duels: feel**
- Your hits land again after a Force push: for 3 seconds after pushing, your swings went through your opponent, which is why hits on a player you had just floored seemed to miss.
- A parry you follow up well is a combo again: if your first return hit connects, the next ones keep their full effect instead of being blockable at once. If they block the first one, they got away with it.
- Being parried now costs 70% of your block stamina instead of half. The meter refills in a few seconds, so two parries in a row broke nobody's guard before.
- The evade kick (attack right after a dodge) still knocks your opponent down but no longer does damage. It is a spacing move, not a free hit.
- Hits show sooner: your opponent's body reacts to a hit the moment their game confirms it, and a blocked or parried hit throws its spark on their blade at once.

## 0.30.4

**Duels**
- Your last placement duel now plays the rank-up ceremony: from unranked, the path lights up from its start to the rank you placed in, and its blade colour is yours.
- The CHARACTER screen says what each reward blade colour was awarded for.

## 0.30.3

**Duel character screen**
- Fixed the game running out of video memory (and closing) after browsing the character screen for a while.
- The screen works with the mouse alone: click a part to open its choices, click a badge to equip it, click a tab to switch. Keys still work as before.
- Trying parts on is smoother: the preview updates once you stop on a part instead of on every step.

## 0.30.2

- The duels test's competitive season is Season 0 until the public release, which starts Season 1. Every screen, title and badge now says Season 0.

## 0.30.1


**Playtest 2: everything since 0.24.5 in one update**

**Co-op story**
- The story goes further: Dathomir and Zeffo are now open in co-op. The playtest ends at Kashyyyk, and the holotable tells you when you get there.
- New BRACCA setting for the host: skip Bracca, each play it on your own, or play it together (still buggy).
- New ONLINE CO-OP menus: invite a friend to your lobby first, then host or join a journey together.

**New: Duels**
- Fight other players one on one: ONLINE CO-OP â€º DUEL. Casual and competitive duels, 14 arenas, Jedi path ranks, rewards and leaderboards.

**Access**
- One build for every tester. HOST JOURNEY / JOIN JOURNEY open with the Journey role and DUEL with the Duelist role. Without the role the entry says LOCKED. Apply with /apply tester in the Jedi Co-op Discord.

**More in co-op**
- The lobby: when the host picks a journey, both of you go straight to it. Leaving the lobby or disbanding a party asks first.
- Hosting and joining a journey shows a picture of the exact area of that save.
- FRIENDS shows each friend's rank and scrolls when the list is long.
- The title screen's ONLINE CO-OP menus are rebuilt to match the game's own menus, with smooth transitions and no more brief stutters.
- Many layout fixes across the co-op menus at every resolution.

**Duels: how they work**
- Ready up, then fight in rounds. A round ends when someone's health bar is empty, they fall out of the ring, or the 3-minute clock runs out (then the player with more health wins the round).
- A 5-second countdown starts every round, and neither player can move before it says DUEL. You both start the same distance from the middle, facing each other.
- Both players get the same health, Force and every skill, with no stims mid-round. Health refills between rounds. Your story saves aren't touched.
- Arenas: the bounty hunters' arena and every Battle Grid arena (about 20 to 25 seconds to load).
- Private duels with a friend: both ready up, choose the arena and the number of rounds, and vote for a rematch.
- If your opponent leaves a duel in any way, you win.

**Duels: competitive**
- Find a Duel: Casual or Competitive, with how many duelists are online, an estimated wait and the leaderboard while you search.
- Competitive opens after 5 casual duels. 5 placement duels set your first rank, from Youngling up to Guardian. Competitive duels are best of 5, casual best of 3.
- Ranks follow the Jedi path, from Youngling to Grand Master. Win streaks move you up faster, losing streaks down faster.
- Each rank unlocks a blade colour to keep: Copper, White, Sapphire, Emerald, Master's Gold and Void Violet. A rank-up ceremony plays when you reach one, and reward colours leave a trail when you swing.
- While the arena loads, you face off: rank badges, titles, frames, card art, records and your head-to-head.
- Leaderboards (global, friends, Europe, North America), your profile (title, frame and card art) and challenges to friends from the leaderboard.
- Seasons: each season ends with a badge and rewards. Master and Grand Master must be earned again every season.
- Discord shows when you're searching for or playing a duel.

**Duels: your character**
- DUEL â€º CHARACTER: build a character just for duels with every outfit, poncho, saber part and BD-1 skin unlocked, with a live preview. Deluxe Edition items need the Deluxe Edition. Your opponent sees your look.

**Duels: fair play**
- Hits only land if your opponent is really within reach, Force push hits when you see it, and you can always get out of a flurry or defend after being parried.
- Competitive needs a Discord sign-in in the launcher, with an account at least 30 days old. One ranked profile per Discord account.
- You can't meet the same player more than 3 times a day in competitive, or someone on your own network. Declining or missing a match means a short wait.
- Report a player from the result screen or their profile. The team reviews every report.
- To stop bans being dodged, duels collect a little extra information when you queue for or play one (never in co-op). The privacy page explains what and why.

**Note**
- Everyone needs 0.30.1 to play together.

## 0.30.0
- The first build of this update, replaced the same day by 0.30.1 (the same update with its last fixes).

## 0.29.4
**Fairer duel starts**
- Neither player can move before the countdown says DUEL, including while the other player is still loading in.
- Both players now start the same distance from the middle of the arena, facing each other, in every arena.
- Your camera starts behind your character, facing your opponent.

## 0.29.3
**Fixes**
- Duels in the Ordo Eris fight pit: the gate to the meditation circle now stays closed, and meditating is switched off during duels.

## 0.29.2
**Duel menus**
- Back (Esc or B on a controller) now goes back one menu at a time instead of leaving the DUEL menus.
- The DUEL menus open and close like the game's own menus, with the same timing, sounds and background blur.
- The menus on the title screen are smoother: less work every frame, and no more brief stutters.
- Match found: Accept is now the bright button, and the player labels no longer cross the ring.
- Small layout fixes on the result, season end, profile and leaderboard screens.

## 0.29.1
**Fair play in ranked duels**
- Competitive needs you to sign in with Discord in the launcher, with a Discord account at least 30 days old. Each Discord account has one ranked profile.
- You can't be matched against the same player more than 3 times a day in competitive, or against someone on your own network.
- Declining or missing a match puts you on a short wait before you can search again.
- You see your opponent's rank and region while accepting; their name and card show once you've both accepted.
- Report a player from the result screen or their profile. The Jedi Co-op team reviews every report and can ban players who cheat. Bans show the reason, how long they last and how to appeal.
- To keep bans from being dodged, duels now collect a little extra information when you queue for or play a duel (never for co-op). The privacy page explains what and why.

**Duels**
- Competitive duels are now best of 5: first to win 3 rounds. Casual duels stay best of 3.
- A 5-second countdown starts every round. Both players are held still until it ends.
- Rounds last 3 minutes. When time runs out, the player with more health wins the round; on equal health the next hit wins. The round clock shows at the top of the screen.
- Much faster loading into Battle Grid arenas: about 20-25 seconds instead of well over a minute. The story arena is a little faster too.
- The loading screen stays up until the arena is ready and both players are in place.
- No co-op pop-ups during duels.
- Fixed a lightsaber showing lit on the hip at the start of a round.
- The ping on the loading screen no longer flickers.
- The DUEL menu has a new PLAY entry for finding, hosting and joining duels, and a fresh look for its screens.

**Note**
- Duelists need 0.29.1 to duel each other.

## 0.29.0
**Ranked duels (duels test)**
- Find a duel from the DUEL menu: Casual or Competitive. Competitive opens after 5 casual duels and starts with 5 placement duels.
- Competitive ranks follow the Jedi path, from Youngling to Grand Master, with three divisions each. Your rating goes up or down after every competitive duel, and you see what's at stake before it starts.
- While the arena loads, both duelists face off: rank badges, titles, frames, card art, records and the head-to-head between you.
- After each duel: your new rating, promotions and anything you unlocked. Competitive has Search again and Leave; casual keeps Rematch.
- Leaderboards (global, friends, Europe, North America) and your profile, where you choose your title, frame and card art.
- Challenge a friend to a duel from the leaderboard.
- Seasons: when a season ends you get its badge and rewards, and everyone starts the next one a little closer to the middle.
- Discord shows that you're in a ranked duel, with your rank.

**Includes everything in 0.28.1.**

**Note**
- Duelists need 0.29.0 to duel each other. It can't join players on other builds.

## 0.28.1
**Co-op fixes**
- Enemies no longer stay on 1 HP after what should have been the killing blow.
- Hardcore: coming back after spectating your partner no longer leaves parts of the map missing (no more falling through the ground).
- Hardcore: the revive timer stops while your partner is reviving you.
- Hardcore: the + over a downed partner shows how many seconds they have left, and a white ring builds around it as you revive them. The + stays on screen when the HUD fades.
- Hardcore: when you're down, you see a ring building as your partner revives you, with their name.

**Note**
- Everyone needs 0.28.1 to play together (co-op journeys too).

## 0.28.0
**Duels: fairer fights**
- Hits only land if your opponent is really within reach on your screen. No more being hit by a swing that looked metres away.
- Force push now hits when you see your opponent push, not before, and always throws you away from them, whichever way you were facing.
- No more stun-lock: after a hit lands, quick follow-up hits still hurt but no longer stagger you, so you can block, parry or roll out of a flurry (the double blade especially).
- Being parried staggers you only briefly, so you can still defend against the counterattack. A parry still drains half your block stamina.
- The health and stamina bars over your opponent no longer jump around, especially during pushes.
- Fixed a crash in the bounty hunters' arena.
- Fixed pushes sometimes also counting as a saber hit.

**Note**
- Everyone needs 0.28.0 to play together (co-op journeys too).

## 0.27.0
**Duels**
- Every Battle Grid arena can now be picked for a duel: 13 in all, plus the bounty hunters' arena. Press Arena in the duel lobby to go through them.
- In Battle Grid arenas you now start in the middle of the arena, facing each other, instead of next to its edge.
- Plays with 0.26.x players.

## 0.26.2
**Duels**
- Fixed a crash that could happen while being taken to a Kashyyyk or Fortress duel.
- You now start each round facing your opponent, with the camera behind you.
- Plays with 0.26.0 and 0.26.1 players.

## 0.26.1
**Duels**
- No stims in duels: nobody can heal mid-round. Health still refills between rounds.
- Fixed the arena suddenly vanishing into empty space during a long duel.
- Picking Kashyyyk or Fortress now reliably takes both of you there. Before, you could end up in different arenas. While you're being taken to the arena your hero stands still; that's expected.
- If your partner's game drops out, the duel is no longer handed to them.
- Plays with 0.26.0 players.

## 0.26.0
**Duels**
- New arenas: the host can pick Kashyyyk or Fortress from the Battle Grid as well as the bounty hunters' arena. Press Arena in the duel lobby to switch; your partner sees the choice straight away. More arenas will follow.
- You can now hear your opponent: their footsteps, their lightsaber and their voice, including when they take a hit.

**Note**
- Everyone needs 0.26.0 to play together (co-op journeys too).

## 0.25.3
**Co-op**
- Enemies fighting your partner no longer block every one of your hits: your hits now count, and they block or parry only when they really do.

**Duels**
- No more stray stormtrooper voices during a duel.
- Round banners play out in full between rounds instead of vanishing.
- Plays with 0.25.0 to 0.25.2 players.

## 0.25.2
**Duels**
- Parrying online is easier: your partner's blows now land when you see their blade reach you, so you can parry by sight whatever the connection.
- Plays with 0.25.0 and 0.25.1 players.

## 0.25.1
**Fixes**
- Duels: the joining player's hits now always reach the host (in a first duel they could miss every time).
- Plays with 0.25.0 players.

## 0.25.0
**New: Duels (advanced testers)**
- Fight your partner one on one in the bounty hunters' arena: Online Co-op > Duel > Host Duel or Join Duel.
- Ready up together, then best of 3 rounds. A round ends when someone's health bar is empty or they fall out of the ring.
- Both players get the same health, Force, stims and every skill. Your own saves aren't touched.
- Single blade hits hardest; the double blade and split sabers hit less per strike but faster. Heavy attacks deal more.
- After the last round: Rematch or Leave.

**Note**
- Everyone needs 0.25.0 to play together (co-op journeys too).

## 0.24.2
**Fixes**
- Your partner's head no longer disappears at times.
- Plays with 0.24.0 and 0.24.1 players.

## 0.24.1
**Fixes**
- Your partner's head shows again (it could be missing, for example in New Journey+).
- Plays with 0.24.0 players.

## 0.24.0
**Story (Dathomir, Zeffo)**
- Story cutscenes wait for you both: a barrier stops whoever arrives first, then the scene starts for both together.
- Zeffo: the tomb's elevator, the cave lights, path-blocking rocks and switches now change for both of you.
- Resting at a meditation circle resets enemies for both players, whoever rests.
- Arriving on a planet together, the landing scene waits for the partner a few seconds behind.

**Fixes**
- Creatures your partner cuts no longer stretch on your screen; the cut parts fall.
- Enemies near you no longer stand frozen when your partner is far away.
- Temple Guardians your partner defeats fall over instead of standing and rattling.
- Rocket and Temple Guardian shots show their trails on your screen.
- Your partner gets the "shortcut unlocked" message too.
- Fewer repeated and leftover pop-ups.
- Both players need this update.

## 0.23.9
**Fixes**
- Enemies your partner kills no longer freeze for a moment before they fall on your screen.
- Bracca: the first-kill tutorial no longer leaves you stuck without a saber, with an invisible saber, or with your
  saber lit on your hip. Each of you makes your own first kill, and the troopers there stay down.
- Bracca train: trooper waves arrive in order for both of you, and no invisible troopers shoot at the host.
- Bracca train: the roof hatch opens for both of you after the "slow an enemy" lesson, even if only one of you used it.
- Bracca: the starfighter scene starts for both of you when one player reaches it another way, and the wing slide
  after it starts a little further down the wing, past the spot players got stuck on.
- Bogano: the lift in the Great Divide no longer crushes a player while the other rides it.
- Your partner no longer goes missing after a flashback, and the game no longer crashes at the end of the wall-run
  flashback.
- Your lock-on lets go of an enemy your partner kills.
- While a cutscene waits for your partner, it stays silent: its voices and music start with the picture.
- Skipping a cutscene waits until the next area has loaded.
- Plays with 0.23.x players.

## 0.23.8
**Fixes**
- No more invisible walls left behind in fights: an enemy that stood in for your partner in your game could leave an
  invisible blocker where it was removed.

## 0.23.7
**Combat**
- Blaster troopers no longer all fire at whoever walked into their range first. A player who arrives later, or keeps
  their distance, counts as part of that fight as soon as they're within the troopers' reach, so the shooters split
  between you and take turns, even if nobody has hit them yet.

## 0.23.6
**Combat**
- Bosses now come to the player they're fighting too: a boss duel runs in that player's own game, so the Second
  Sister (and other bosses) attack you, react to your hits and lock sabers with you whether you host or join. Their
  scripted moments play for both of you as before.

## 0.23.5
**Fixes**
- An enemy your partner kills no longer stands still for a moment on your screen before it falls (a wait added in
  0.23.0 for finishers now only applies while a finisher is actually playing).

## 0.23.4
**Combat**
- An enemy that comes for you now runs in your own game, whichever of you is hosting: it reacts to your hits at once
  and swings at where you are, not at where you were a moment ago. Your partner sees the same enemy on their screen as
  before.
- Enemies now count you as part of a fight when you're in it, not only once you've landed damage, so they spread
  between you in fights where you're mostly deflecting and parrying.
- Enemies change hands between the two games less often.

## 0.23.3
**Fixes**
- Your partner's enemies, and your partner as their enemies see them, were drawn up to 150 ms behind even on a fast
  connection, which made hits land late and swings miss. Enemies now settle at the delay the connection needs
  (about 90 ms on a good link) and drop to it quickly when they close in.

## 0.23.2
**Hotfix**
- Fixed a crash in the Dathomir hallway when the cutscene there started. Now, if you get there first, the way on stays
  shut with WAITING FOR until your partner catches up, then the cutscene plays for both of you.
- Plays with 0.23.0 and 0.23.1 players.

## 0.23.1
**Combat**
- Blaster troopers and other shooters now split between the two of you as well, and swap targets every few seconds
  while you both fight them, instead of all firing at one player for the whole fight (the Bracca train, for one).

## 0.23.0
**Combat**
- Enemies now split themselves between the two of you. A group that joins a fight no longer piles onto whoever got
  there first: each new enemy goes to the player with fewer on them, and enemies rotate between you while you both
  fight the same group.
- Enemies find your partner more reliably: the fix for the cases where every enemy kept fighting one player for a
  long stretch of a fight.
- The block bar under an enemy's health is now the same on both screens. Your partner's hits deplete it on your
  screen too.
- Finishers performed by your partner play out fully on your screen, and the enemy ends in the pose the finisher
  left it in, instead of dropping into a plain death halfway through.
- Enemies your partner cuts in two now show the cut on your screen as well, including the creatures whose severed
  parts are separate pieces. A cut that doesn't kill no longer makes the body stretch and twist on the other screen.
- Enemies that only one of you had (ones a level script or scene brings in, rather than a regular spawn point) now
  appear for the other player too, so nobody is seen fighting thin air. Enemy groups the other player sets off now
  appear for you even if your side of that area loads a while later.
- Both players need this update (it changes what the two games send each other).

## 0.22.3
**Fixes**
- The co-op lobby no longer says "Europe" for every player. Once your partner joins, it shows which region your
  connection goes through (North America or Europe), next to your ping.

## 0.22.2
**Fixes**
- Skipping a cutscene now fades out only that cutscene's voices and music. The level's music and ambience keep playing.
- Skipping a cutscene that leads straight into another no longer freezes or silences the next one.
- Skipping while a cutscene waits for your partner now needs both of you, and the skipped cutscene doesn't play again.
- BD-1's repair on Bogano now waits until both of you are past the fan. Before, a partner still behind it could be
  pulled into the fan.
- Fixed getting stuck on debris at the top of the starfighter wing slide.
- Hardcore: holding X on a controller next to your downed partner revives them without swinging your lightsaber.
- Hardcore: the first boss fight on Bracca plays as normal. Getting low on health there no longer puts you down.
- Plays with 0.22.0 and 0.22.1 players.

## 0.22.1
**Hotfix**
- Skipping a cutscene now stops its sound too. Before, its voices and music played on for several seconds.
- Plays with 0.22.0 players.

## 0.22.0
**Story cutscenes wait for both of you**
- Big story cutscenes now wait until both of you are there. Whoever gets there first keeps playing: explore, or go
  back for your partner. You see "WAITING FOR" with your partner's name, and once they're close the cutscene starts
  for both of you at the same moment.
- A cutscene you start by pressing something (the console in the train before Cal's vision) waits until both of you
  have pressed it.
- At the end of the train, the way up onto the roof stays shut until your partner catches up, so the escape plays for
  both of you together.
- Everything else works as before: things that change the world (platforms, ledges, doors) happen for both of you when
  you're together and for each of you on your own when you're apart. Voice lines and camera moves only play for the
  player who set them off. Bracca's opening, up to the train, plays exactly as before.
- Your partner is hidden while you slide down the starfighter's wing and hang in the cables, and after the fall
  through the train until one of you swings your lightsaber.
- After you skip a cutscene, skipping is off for 10 seconds (skipping twice in a row could play the scene again).
- Fixed co-op stopping during the fall from the train.
- Known issue: skipping a cutscene doesn't stop its sound yet.
- This build only plays with other 0.22.0 players.

**Hardcore mode (new for early access)**
- A new co-op setting, HARDCORE, in the co-op settings (and the lobby's CO-OP SETTINGS, changeable at any time). The
  join screen shows when a journey is hardcore.
- Fall in battle and you're down, not dead. A + shows over you, and your partner has 20 seconds to reach you and hold
  Interact (E, or X on a controller) for 3 seconds to get you back up with half your health. "HOLD E TO REVIVE" (X on
  a controller) appears when they're close enough. Enemies leave you alone while you're down, and a hit on your partner
  stops the revive. Shots and acid can put you down too, not only melee hits.
- Going down puts your lightsaber out; it lights again when you draw it after getting up. Your partner's status line
  says Down or Spectating instead of the distance.
- If nobody reaches you in time, you spectate: you see exactly what your partner sees, with their health and stims
  under the status chip. Press E (X on a controller) to look around on your own, and again to go back to their view.
  Spectating costs the XP a death costs, as in the normal game, and you can win it back the same way.
- When your partner rests at a meditation circle, your screen fades to black and you come back in the meditation menu
  at their circle, rested and saved, as if you had rested there too. Their circle is then where you'd come back next
  time. Enemies don't respawn a second time when you come back.
- If you both fall, it's the game's own death for both of you, back at your last rest. When you aren't playing
  together (your partner is on another planet or not connected), a fall is the game's own death as usual.
- Leaving the session while you're down or spectating puts you back on your feet with your controls and the normal
  screen.

## 0.21.3
**A co-op server in North America (advanced test build)**
- When two players in North or South America can't connect to each other directly, co-op now goes through a new
  server in North America instead of the one in Europe. That cuts the lag for them noticeably.
- The co-op lobby shows "relay NA" or "relay EU" next to your partner's ping when you're connected through one.
- Plays with 0.21.1 and 0.21.2 players too (they connect the way they did before).

## 0.21.2
**Hardcore mode fixes (advanced test build)**
- Coming back after your partner rests now always takes you to their circle. If you had gone down standing next to a
  different circle, you could be sent to that one instead and end up under the map.
- If your partner's circle hasn't loaded on your side yet, you wait on the black screen a little longer. If it still
  isn't there, you come back where you fell instead of falling through the world.
- Your partner resting no longer respawns the enemies a second time when you come back.
- While you're coming back after a rest, enemies no longer target you before you can see.
- A killing blow from an enemy's shot or acid now puts you down like any other hit. Before, it could do nothing.
- The moment after a revive is safe from shots and acid too, not only from melee hits.
- Going down and being left to spectate now costs the XP a death costs, as in the normal game, and you can win it back
  the same way.
- Leaving the session while you're down or spectating puts you back on your feet with your controls and the normal
  screen. Before, you could be left invisible and unable to use meditation circles or chests until you restarted the
  game.
- Enemies no longer attack a downed partner's body.
- "HOLD X TO REVIVE" and the spectate camera switch show X when you play with a controller.
- Holding Interact to revive someone next to a chest no longer opens the chest, and the pause menu stops the revive.
- The join screen shows when a journey is hardcore (once the JediCoop server is updated).
- This build plays with 0.21.1 players.

## 0.21.1
**Hardcore mode, round two (advanced test build)**
- When your partner is down, a + shows over them, and "HOLD E TO REVIVE" appears under it when you're close enough.
  Their status line says Down or Spectating instead of the distance.
- Going down puts your lightsaber out. Once you're back on your feet, it lights again when you draw it.
- While you spectate, you see exactly what your partner sees, camera and all. Press E (X on a controller) to look
  around on your own instead, and again to go back to their view. The world turns grey for a moment as you start
  watching, then back to its normal colour.
- A spectating player no longer shows next to the player they're watching, or on the map.
- When your partner rests, your screen fades to black and you come back in the meditation menu at their circle, rested
  and saved. You leave it like any meditation.
- While your partner is in the meditation menu, you see them at the circle.
- Reviving someone no longer brings an enemy with it.
- Your partner's stims now show while you spectate them.
- This build only plays with other 0.21.1 players.

## 0.21.0
**Hardcore mode (advanced test build)**
- A new co-op setting, HARDCORE, in the co-op settings (and the lobby's CO-OP SETTINGS, changeable at any time).
- Fall in battle and you're down, not dead: your partner has 20 seconds to reach you and hold Interact (E, or X on a
  controller) for 3 seconds to get you back on your feet with half your health. Enemies leave you alone while you're

- If you both fall, it's the game's own death for both of you, back at your last rest.
- When you aren't playing together (your partner is on another planet or not connected), a fall is the game's own
  death as usual.
- This build only plays with other 0.21.0 players.

**Fixes**
- A crash that could follow when both players died at around the same time.

## 0.20.2

## 0.20.0

first visit to Bogano. Here's everything that's changed since 0.18.0.

**Playing the story together**
- Cutscenes start at the same moment for both of you when you're together. Apart, each of you sees them when you get
  there, and your partner's world isn't changed before they arrive.
- Skip cutscenes together: hold Esc (Y / Triangle on a controller) during a cutscene and your half of the ring in the
  corner fills. When your partner holds too, it skips for both of you. A cutscene only you are watching skips once your
  hold fills the ring.
- Story moments only wait for your partner when they need to. Voice lines, hints, tutorial pop-ups, camera moves and
  music happen straight away for whoever reaches them.
- Set pieces, platforms, doors and the train's cables happen for both of you when you're close together.
- Clamps need both of you when you're together; apart, each of you works your own. One of you opens a door panel for
  both, and tutorial prompts done by one of you count for both.
- Bracca's train plays out together: its doors, consoles, tutorials, the gunship and the grunts from the hatch.
- The Second Sister: her final clash starts for both of you at the same moment, and you both do the button mash.
- Dying in a set piece you did together brings you back next to your partner, past it.
- BD-1's repair, the scene before it and BD-1's heal start together when you're close.
- When the story sends you on from Bogano, the Mantis holotable shows "The playtest ends here". Journeys further into
  the story are greyed out for this playtest; start a new co-op journey together.

**Co-op menus and friends**

  and a countdown that lights the ring.
- Friends: everyone has a tag (like Ezm#4821). Add friends, see who's online and what they're doing, ask to join a
  friend who's hosting, and invite friends from your lobby with no code to type.
- The join screen shows the host's co-op settings, including whether chest cosmetics are each player's own or the
  same for both.
- Mouse and controller fixes across the co-op menus.

**Enemies and combat**
- Enemies stay in step between your games: no bobbing, no jumps when you meet up again, and no flying off when killed.
- Blaster bolts fired at you hit, get blocked or get deflected as in single player.
- Force Pull, Push and Slow on an enemy your partner was fighting respond straight away.
- Bosses keep their damage when one of you dies, and fight the player who comes back.
- You hear the enemies fighting your partner, and cut-up enemies look right on both screens.

**The world**
- Moving platforms, spinning fans, ropes you cut down and other moving parts of the levels stay the same for both of
  you.
- The lift on Bogano no longer kills you partway up.

**Fixes**
- Fixed crashes: a friend joining with lightsaber parts the host doesn't have, BD-1's heal with your partner far away,
  the Dathomir hallway cutscene, and a friends update arriving while a save loaded.
- Fixed the mod switching itself off during the jump to hyperspace.

## 0.9.0
The first version with the JediCoop launcher and join codes.

**Getting started**
- The JediCoop launcher finds your game (Steam or EA app), checks it's a supported version, and
  installs, updates or removes the mod with one click. It never changes the game's own files.
- Set your name once in the launcher; press Play to start the game with JediCoop.
- Back up your saves, or import a save a friend sent you, from the launcher.

**Play together**
- Host: press F6 in the game. You get a join code (like K7Q-X9R), already copied: paste it to your
  friend. No extra software or router settings needed.
- Join: copy the code, then press F7 in the game (or press F7 and type it).
- See your friend's Cal in your game, with lightsaber, poncho and BD-1.
- Fight together: shared enemies, damage and deaths in both games; blaster bolts, acid spit and
  baton strikes from enemies the other game runs hit you too, with the game's own knockback and
  sparks. Block bolts to stop them.
- Travel separately: each player flies their own Mantis. When one picks a planet, the other is
  asked "Follow? [Y] / [N]".
- Shared world: a shortcut door unlocked by one player opens for both; Force Slow on a puzzle
  object slows it in both games.
- Difficulty: Co-op (the normal game) or Scaled (tougher enemies for two players).

**Menus and messages**
- F4 opens the co-op menu (session, join code, keys, your name, difficulty, mod version).
- Join problems are explained: a wrong code, or a different mod or game version, says so plainly.

**Safety**
- Back up your saves from the launcher before playing together (one click, dated copies).

**Known limits**
- Force Slow on an object looks different in the other player's game.
- Parrying a bolt back only works for bolts aimed at you.
- Enemies alerted far from one player may stand still in that player's game until they're defeated.
- Some enemy types and bosses are untested.
